title: Evaporative Emissions: Choosing the Diagnostic Route
introduction:
EVAP manages fuel vapor so it can be used by the engine instead of escaping freely. I think of it as fuel-vapor housekeeping: its plumbing and control valves handle a different task from the liquid fuel supply.

Here, the useful decision is whether the driveability complaint has a diagnostic trouble code attached. This page points to the appropriate diagnostic reference. Continuing the diagnosis requires that reference's setup and tests, which are not included here.

edits.why: Code-based and symptom-based diagnosis begin in different references.

edits.text: If a PCM DTC—a diagnostic trouble code from the powertrain control module—is present, refer to Electronic Engine Controls (303-14D Electronic Engine Controls - 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: The code provides the starting point for the referenced diagnostic work. It is a clue to investigate, rather than a replacement-parts shopping list.

edits.text: For driveability symptoms without a DTC, refer to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED) manual. Use Section 3, Symptom Charts, to enter the symptom-based diagnostic route.
edits.why: A symptom can need investigation even when no code accompanies it. The symptom charts provide the original next branch for that situation.
